newsitem.title: USA: Home Shopping's Diller sees higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Home Shopping's Diller sees higher profits.

text.p: Home Shopping Network Inc Chairman Barry Diller said Monday the electronic retailer expected earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) to reach a run rate of $100 million by the end of the year.

"We will be there," he said, referring to the company's 1996 target for annualized EBITDA growth. He said the network's management was "confident (of achieving) a $150 million run rate in 1997 at some point, hopefully beyond that."
In the first half of 1996, HSN posted EBITDA of $29.1 million, compared with a $10.7 million loss before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization in the first half of 1995.

In a company presentation at a Montgomery Securities investment conference in San Francisco, Kevin McKeon, executive vice president and chief executive officer of Home Shopping Network, said that "for the balance of the year the company expects to see margins improved" as it implemented a strategy of reducing prices of items sold to less than $50 each.
For all of 1995, HSN posted a loss before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $25 million and a $0.57 loss per share fully diluted.
Montgomery analysts project EBIDTA will rise to $69 million in 1996 and $132 million in 1997.
